name: Pinboard
tagline: Run a fast private bookmark archive with tags, notes, and full-text search

pricing.notes: Annual account price divided by 12; archival add-on costs extra.

tiers.name: Regular account
tiers.limits: Private bookmark archive with tags and notes; imports are capped at 40 MB/file.

tiers.name: Archiving account
tiers.limits: Regular features plus saved page copies and full-text search.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier and no trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: multi-year discounts may be offered at checkout but the current discount schedule is not published

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Pinboard, run a fast private bookmark archive with tags, notes, and full-text search. The hard boundary is hosted longevity, simple api, archive service, and zero-maintenance reliability, plus capture polish, sync, and content partnerships.
coreLoopDIY: Save permitted web pages into a fast private bookmark archive, extract readable text, tag and annotate entries, search full text, and export the archive in open formats.
whatYouLose: hosted longevity, simple API, archive service, and zero-maintenance reliability
moatNotes: capture polish, sync, and content partnerships
ongoingBurden: feed quirks, parsing, paywalls, canonical URLs, deduplication, images, search, sync, browser extensions, and publisher changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pinboard because people pay when capture works everywhere, reading state syncs instantly, and the archive remains clean without constant parser repairs. The recurring cost buys feed quirks, parsing, paywalls, canonical URLs, deduplication, images, search, sync, browser extensions, and publisher changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: FreshRSS
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source RSS reader with feeds, filters, and self-hosting support.

alternatives.name: Karakeep
alternatives.desc: Bookmarks, notes, full-text search and automatic tags for people with too many tabs.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack for the free self-hosted route, or a hosted Karakeep Cloud signup
facts.engines: Automatic tagging and OCR can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Azure OpenAI, or a local Ollama model; Tesseract is the default non-LLM OCR path.
facts.dataFormat: Bookmarks and metadata live in SQLite under the persistent data directory; page screenshots, PDFs, readable text, and uploads live on local or S3-compatible storage, with Meilisearch indexes in its own volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Karakeep is far heavier than Pinboard's fast text-first archive and requires more storage, background services, maintenance, and interface overhead for a simple tag-and-search job.
facts.setupBlocker: The free route needs Docker Compose, persistent secrets and volumes, a browser worker/Chrome, Meilisearch, HTTPS, backups, and optionally an API key or Ollama for AI features.

alternatives.name: LinkAce
alternatives.desc: A sober tag-and-list bookmark archive that checks whether links have died.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack for self-hosting, or a paid managed/one-click host
facts.dataFormat: Links, lists, tags, notes, users, and status checks live in MariaDB/MySQL; the application, search, cache, and backup files live in persistent volumes, while archival references can point to the Internet Archive rather than a local page copy.
facts.gapVsPaid: LinkAce is slower and more operationally complex than Pinboard and does not preserve a full searchable copy of every saved page by default.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting starts with a multi-service stack, Docker, MariaDB, Meilisearch, Redis, scheduled jobs, HTTPS, backups, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: linkding
alternatives.desc: Pinboard with a nicer face and no annual invoice.

facts.install: Run the single official Docker container and create the first superuser
facts.dataFormat: Bookmarks, tags, notes, users, and metadata live in a persistent SQLite database by default or PostgreSQL; the optional plus image stores locally captured HTML snapshots and browser data in the mounted data directory.
facts.gapVsPaid: linkding is close to Pinboard's core but lacks the same long-lived hosted simplicity and requires the user to operate synchronization, backups, and optional page archiving.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker and a persistent data volume are the first hurdle; reliable local page archiving requires the larger Chromium-equipped plus image rather than the standard lightweight image.

alternatives.name: Linkwarden
alternatives.desc: A private bookmark archive that also keeps searchable copies of what you saved.

facts.install: Hosted signup or the official Docker Compose self-hosting stack
facts.engines: Automatic tagging can use Ollama, OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or Perplexity.
facts.dataFormat: Collections, links, tags, users, and annotations live in PostgreSQL; screenshots, PDFs, readable archives, previews, and uploads live on local persistent storage or configured S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Linkwarden offers richer archiving but is substantially heavier than Pinboard and makes the user maintain PostgreSQL, storage, browser capture, and backups.
facts.setupBlocker: The indefinitely free route requires Docker, PostgreSQL, authentication secrets, persistent archive storage, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, backups, and upgrades.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Regular account plan and a personal reading archive DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Pinboard in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, Readability.js, and a local background worker; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: save permitted web pages into a fast private bookmark archive, extract readable text, tag and annotate entries, search full text, and export the archive in open formats.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support manual URL save, RSS or Atom subscriptions, OPML import, and a simple bookmarklet.
Fetch politely with a clear user agent, rate limits, conditional requests, and robots-aware behavior.
Extract title, author, date, canonical URL, readable HTML, and selected images.
Provide inbox, unread, archive, favorites, tags, highlights, notes, and full-text search.
Keep the original URL prominent and never attempt to bypass authentication or paywalls.
Export OPML, bookmarks HTML, Markdown, and a complete JSON backup.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out paywall circumvention.
Deliberately leave out licensed publisher content and recommendation networks.
Deliberately leave out native mobile clients and seamless commercial sync.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
